chapters.title: Two Computers, One Tree
chapters.blurb: One React tree is pulled apart across a physical gap — server components dissolve into their output while the use client counter seals shut and crosses as a reference.

chapters.title: Rows on a Tape
chapters.blurb: Flight's actual wire format: hex-addressed, newline-framed rows, the element tuple, dollar-prefixed references, and a tape you can read before it finishes writing.

chapters.title: The Customs Gate
chapters.blurb: Every prop walks through a customs gate: dates, maps and promises morph into their encodings; functions and class instances bounce with React's real error text.

chapters.title: Chunks That Wake Up
chapters.blurb: On the client, every row id gets a promise-like chunk cell — the page stands up with suspense holes that pop as cells flip to fulfilled.

chapters.title: The Wire Runs Backwards
chapters.blurb: Server actions run the wire in reverse: a stamped reference dials home, arguments pass the same gate, and a plain form still posts with scripting off.
